title: Evaluation of the canonical proper singleton mate is the scalar projection inverse
statement: Let O be a commutative ring, t an element, f:X→Y a scheme morphism, c a compactification and S:StrictEtaleCompactSupport O t c [def-per-strict-etale-system-interfaces]. Fix m≤n and a natural isomorphism q from scalar extension on c.Z followed by level-m proper direct image to level-n proper direct image followed by scalar extension on Y. Suppose q.inv is exactly the geometric mate of S.properDerived.derivedTensor at m≤n. Form insertion by conjugating S.properDerived.directEvaluation at level n under the composite singleton/geometric adjunctions, and then form its proper mate a. For every P in the derived category at level n on c.Z, evaluation at m of a(P), followed by the proper directEvaluation comparison and the level-m direct image of the singleton derivedBelow comparison on c.Z, equals the singleton derivedBelow comparison on Y at the level-n direct image of P followed by q.inv at P. No finite coefficient hypothesis and no singleton invertibility assumption are imposed.

source.place: Zheng, Lemma 5.13 (printed pp. 34–35): evaluation of (4.10.2) as coefficient projection, with the singleton Hom-transpose normalization of Construction 4.1.

proof.text: Apply derivedMate_comparison to the ordinary singleton/scalar square, using hom_formula at the identity, transpose, scalar.transpose and transition_rep. Its representative equation agrees with derivedBelow_rep after the recorded belowComplex_f equation. Postcompose the resulting mate with derivedBelow.hom and apply the scalar left-derived universal property to identify it with the identity. Thus derivedBelow.inv is exactly the mate of the derived transition, for the supplied package, without comparing with a separately chosen model.

Apply iterated_mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv to the insertion square. Inverse conjugation identifies its iterated mate with directEvaluation.inv. The singleton mate-transpose identity then says that the singleton transpose of a, followed by directEvaluation at n, is the proper direct image of the singleton unit.

Use the geometric mate-counit identity for q.inv and the restrictedDirect_mate equation. After cancelling the tensor comparison, the scalar unit naturality and the geometric triangle identity show that the scalar transpose of q.inv is the level-n proper direct image of the scalar unit followed by restrictedDirect.

Precompose the claimed equality with derivedBelow.inv on Y and apply the scalar Hom equivalence. The below-level transpose identity, directTransition, the insertion identity and naturality of restrictedDirect reduce the left side to the proper direct image of the scalar unit followed by restrictedDirect. The same scalar-unit calculation identifies the right side. Cancel the invertible below-level comparison and use injectivity of the Hom equivalence.

lean.statement:
theorem etaleBrownProperSingletonEvaluation
    (S : StrictEtaleCompactSupport O t c) {m n : ℕ} (h : m ≤ n)
    (q : (S.PZ.scalar h).derived ⋙ (S.properDerived.level m).direct ≅
      (S.properDerived.level n).direct ⋙ (S.PY.scalar h).derived)
    (hq : q.inv =
      (mateEquiv (S.properDerived.level n).adjunction (S.properDerived.level m).adjunction
        (.mk _ _ _ _ (S.properDerived.derivedTensor h).hom)).natTrans)
    (P : DerivedCategory (strictEtaleLevel c.Z O t n)) :
    let insertion := ((conjugateIsoEquiv
      ((S.PY.derivedAdj n).comp S.properDerived.system.adjunction)
      (((S.properDerived.level n).adjunction).comp (S.PZ.derivedAdj n))).symm
        (S.properDerived.directEvaluation n)).symm
    let a := (mateEquiv (S.properDerived.level n).adjunction
      S.properDerived.system.adjunction (.mk _ _ _ _ insertion.hom)).natTrans
    (S.PY.evaluation m).map (a.app P) ≫
      (S.properDerived.directEvaluation m).hom.app ((S.PZ.derivedExtension n).obj P) ≫
      (S.properDerived.level m).direct.map ((S.PZ.derivedBelow h).hom.app P) =
    (S.PY.derivedBelow h).hom.app ((S.properDerived.level n).direct.obj P) ≫
      q.inv.app P
